title: Bandwidth shepherd calendar and safety checks (2027-04)
content:
Purpose:
A compact working-plan to drive the Bandwidth Shepherd rollout for the new request-throttling shim in front of the serving runtime. Focus: minimize tail-latency regressions while validating token accounting and cost-sampling. This is intentionally terse — quick checklist + calendar + release notes draft for the on-call and deploy crew.

Context/constraints:
- New per-customer smoothing/burst algorithm (v1) merged to staging branch on 2027-04-10.
- Affects request admission and early-drop behavior; observable changes expected in 99th pct tail and queue-fill metrics.
- Backwards compatible with existing Client SDKs; feature gated by org flag and rollout policy.
- Production weekdays: prefer 06:00–18:00 PT windows for initial micro-rollouts.

Contacts:
- Primary owner: Aisha Patel (pager: aisha_p)
- Secondary: Marco Ruiz (pager: marco_r)
- On-call SRE: Samira Cho (rotate)
- Optics/Telemetry lead: Devin O'Neal

Quick rollout calendar (compact):
- T+0 (Mon 2027-04-19 09:00 PT): Canary gate — deploy to canary cluster (canary-1) with traffic tag rollout=bandwidth-shepherd; initial traffic fraction 0.5% (internal only + low-traffic customers). 1h soak.
- T+0 + 6h: Evaluate telem. If clear, escalate to 3% for 2h.
- T+1 (Mon 2027-04-20 09:00 PT): Expand to 12% (regional split: us-west/us-central) for 6h.
- T+2 (Tue 2027-04-21 09:00 PT): Ramp to 35% for 12h with additional edge regions (eu-west).
- T+3 (Wed 2027-04-22 09:00 PT): 80% for 24h (monitor closely); then full 100% night window if stable.
- Rollout notes: each step must pass smoke+metrics gates before advancing. If any gate fails, immediate rollback to previous fraction and 1h freeze for postmortem decisions.

Safety and gating checklist (short):
- Deployment prep:
  - [ ] Confirm canary image tag matching artifact registry: runtimes:sha-2034b
  - [ ] Validate config: smoothing-window=30s, burst-multiplier=2 (defaults in staging.yml)
  - [ ] Confirm feature-flag state and kill-switch route available in console (flag: bandwidth_shepherd_v1)
  - [ ] Green CI: unit/integration for admission logic (PR #789 status: merged -> passing in staging)
  - [ ] Run local load harness against canary to exercise drop-paths (target qps 800, 95th token seq 256)

- Preflight telemetry checks (before moving past any step):
  - P95 latency change <= +20% absolute and <= +10% relative compared to baseline (last 7d)
  - P99 latency delta flagged and must be within +50ms absolute or explained by legitimate queueing (ops note)
  - Error rate (5xx) must remain <= baseline +0.05% absolute
  - Early-drop events rate tracked; expected 0.02%–0.2% at 0.5% traffic, linear-ish growth as fraction rises — any jump > 3x expected triggers rollback
  - Token accounting divergence (billing sampling check): less than 1% delta vs baseline sampling run
  - Queue-length (per-node) should not exceed 0.8 * configured capacity for >5 minutes
  - Cost sampling probes: synthetic traces inserted at 10m cadence; verify cost per-token delta within acceptable band

- Smoke tests (run immediately after each deployment step):
  - [ ] auth handshake + token refresh (happy path) -> < 200ms
  - [ ] simple generation (prompt="hi") -> success, length 20
  - [ ] long-context generation (seq 2048) -> observe memory spike and KV-cache metrics (no OOM)
  - [ ] policy-enforced rejection path (large prompt causing early-drop) -> graceful 429 with diagnostic header
  - [ ] CDN/cache warm path: small request repeated 10x -> no S3 misses in backend logs

Rollback triggers (immediate):
- Any sustained 5xx increase > 0.1% absolute over 15m window
- P99 latency regression unexplained by known traffic or scheduled maintenance and > +200ms absolute
- Early-drop surge > 3x predicted for current traffic fraction
- Billing/sample token divergence > 2% for two consecutive probes
- Any customer-severity incident (P0/P1) reported in first 30 minutes after ramp

Rollback steps (fast):
1) Flip kill-switch for feature flag (bandwidth_shepherd_v1 = false) via console (fast path).
2) If flag flip unresponsive, revert routing at ingress LB to previous canary tag (route: canary-1 -> canary-0).
3) Post-rollback: snapshot logs (last 60m) and create immediate incident stub (template REL-ROLLBACK-STUB) and notify on-call and product.

Post-advance checks (after each step):
- [ ] Run full tracing sample (100 traces) to ensure no spans > 1s in admission path
- [ ] Confirm downstream model-serving pods did not observe token loss or repeated replays
- [ ] Confirm KMS/HSM calls for key retrieval remain within baseline latencies

Telemetry dashboards to watch (links & panels):
- Admission-service: p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, drop-rate panel
- Platform-cost: per-token sample, cost-per-request sampler
- Error budget: 5xx headroom panel
- Release-health: canary -> production mapping with traffic fractions and roll-forward history
(see linked Confluence page above for dashboard shortlinks)

Release notes (draft - to ship with rollout):
Title: Bandwidth Shepherd v1 - adaptive smoothing and burst control
Summary: Introduces an admission-time smoothing layer designed to reduce sudden queue pressure and spread bursts more evenly across nodes. The feature improves system stability under spikey client traffic and provides fine-grained early-drop telemetry for planning cost/latency tradeoffs.
What changed:
- New admission shim between ingress and runtime that applies per-org smoothing windows and token-bucket bursts.
- Configurable parameters: smoothing-window, burst-multiplier, early-drop-thresholds. Default set conservatively.
- Added telemetry hooks for early-drops and billing-sample alignment.
Impact and risk:
- Expected positive: lower P99 in spike scenarios, fewer node OOMs during flash events.
- Known risks: may increase P95 slightly in steady-state due to buffering; token-accounting sampling must be verified (see regression checks).
How to opt-out:
- Customers can be excluded by toggling the flag in the Console (Support -> Feature Flags -> bandwidth_shepherd_v1) or via support request.
Release contacts:
- Release engineer: Aisha Patel; Product owner: Marco Ruiz; SRE lead: Samira Cho.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Q: Should smoothing-window default be 30s or 10s for low-latency apps? Add perf test comparing 10/30/60s.
- Q: Are there customers with contract clauses that forbid early-drop (billing)? Need legal check on opt-out workflow.
- TODO: Add automated rollback playbook to Console buttons (ticket: ENG-1308).
- TODO: Finalize canary image pinning to immutable artifact in infra registry (follow-up with infra: PR #802).

Field notes and fragments (raw):
- if SAMs spike at 11:34 -> consider hard throttle on orgs > 95th percentile qps
- watch for repeated 429 with header 'x-rw-drop-reason' - that identifies early-drop path vs upstream errors
- stamp: if canary is stable for 36h -> propose opt-in rollout to dedicated customers as preview cohort

End of doc — keep light and iterative. If we hit any gate, stop the calendar and convene the cross-team 15m sync (owner + SRE + Product + Observability).
